### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **0** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a61f61a46ea4cf33ed2edce9af0989a668e75f10` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

### ① Derived judgments

**The budget is the sibling's shape, and 60 s is the right value.** `operation-private-keys.pin.test.ts` on `main` declares `const SCAN_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000;` under a docblock and passes it as each `it`'s last argument; this PR does the same thing by the same name, value and position in the sibling file, one directory over, with a docblock that gives its own reason. No vitest config in the chain sets `testTimeout` (`vitest.preset.mts`, `packages/core/vitest.config.ts`), so the pin ran at the 5000 ms default. The timeout the body cites is real and is not the dev's account: the first attempt of `Test Core (2/8)` on the sibling PR's head `c97eb416db`, started 2026-11-07T08:36Z, ends with `Test timed out in 5000ms` at `vouched-reference-callers.pin.test.ts:39:3`, the `--ts-only` case, with the file at 6255 ms; the re-run of the same job passed. 60 s is about ten times the loaded reading and the same headroom the sibling chose for the same kind of runner. It hides no slowness: the file-level wall gate (`measure-test-shard-timings`, the 10 s line and the `// test-budget:` header) grades the file's duration independently and report-only, so a scan that really grows still surfaces there; what the budget removes is a red that says nothing about the mark, raised before any assertion runs. The self-test case gets the same budget on a stated reason (same process start, same runner), which is how the sibling applies its constant too. Clocked windows measure behaviour here, not loading: the test spawns the census and clocks the scan, so `check:test-source-alias`'s convention is untouched.

**The inputs are complete and nothing extra is declared.** The census's import closure on `main` is `./invoked-as.mjs` and `./js-comment-mask.mjs`, and `js-comment-mask.mjs` itself imports `./invoked-as.mjs`; beyond that only node builtins. Its file set comes from `git ls-files` under the scan roots, which with `--ts-only` is the `.ts` surface of `packages/` already declared as `packages/**/*.ts`. `js-comment-mask.d.mts` is not loaded by an `.mjs` importer and is rightly left out. Both helpers are added to the `@objectstack/core` globs in `scripts/cross-package-test-inputs.mjs` and to `@objectstack/core#test:repo` inputs in `turbo.json`, spelled exactly as the `build` and `*#build` tasks on `main` already spell them. Layer C holds without an edit: ci.yml's `core` filter lists both files by name and `crosspkg` carries `scripts/**`, and the head's `filter` check-run is green.

**The `heldBy` witness is honest under the gate's dispositions.** `globHolderVerdict` holds a glob mechanically when a path an escaping test quotes lands in it, or by declaration when `heldBy` names a test that is still one of the package's escaping tests. The pin quotes only the census path, so no quoted path lands in either helper; the read is real because the spawned child loads both and their bytes move the pin's verdict. That is the gate's second disposition (a read the scan cannot name), and the entry's comment says plainly that the child, not the pin, loads them. The witness is checked in the failing direction: the pin is an escaping test only through its `resolve(HERE, '../../../../scripts/...')` seed, so if it stopped escaping the glob would fail by name rather than sit declared and unheld. The table already carries a precedent for declaring an import rather than a file read (the cli entry's `js-comment-mask.mjs`).

**`skip-changeset` is right.** The diff is one `*.test.ts` in `@objectstack/core`, which publishes `dist` only, plus root `turbo.json` and `scripts/`, neither of which is published. Nothing a consumer installs moves. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are the correct declarations, and the `Check Changeset` run on the head is green.

**No required context and no test behaviour changes.** The two assertions are byte-identical to `main`; only the budget argument is added. No workflow, no `.claude/**`, no `skills/**`, no ADR, no spec. The head repo is the base repo, so this is a delivery, not a fork proposal. The Governed Surface Queue Guard on the head is green.

- Should-fix, not blocking: the detector cannot follow a spawned root script's import closure, which is why a witness was needed at all. The `dispatch-gates` derivation already follows a gate's first-party imports one level; a card to teach `check-cross-package-test-inputs` the same hop would let these two globs be held mechanically and retire the witness. File it; do not widen this PR for it.
